lesson.title: Build Your First Neural Network with TensorFlow

goalMatch.note: This video walks you through coding, training and testing a basic neural network on MNIST with TensorFlow, which directly matches building a neural network, though the example is a simple beginner one

sources.title: Build Your First Neural Network with TensorFlow

steps.title: Create venv and start Jupyter
steps.instructions: In an empty project folder, create and activate a venv, then pip install jupyter, tensorflow, numpy and matplotlib. Launch Jupyter Notebook and create a new Python 3 notebook.

targets.caption: Install packages inside the activated venv

explanations.topic: Using a virtual environment and Jupyter Notebook

hints: Make sure your virtual environment is active before installing packages.
Run `source venv/bin/activate` so `(venv)` appears in your terminal prompt.
Run `pip3 install jupyter tensorflow numpy matplotlib` followed by `jupyter notebook`, then click New -> Python 3 (ipykernel).
common_mistakes: Installing packages globally before activating the virtual environment.
Forgetting to select the Python 3 (ipykernel) kernel when creating the new notebook.
steps.run_command: python3 -m venv venv && source venv/bin/activate && pip3 install jupyter tensorflow numpy matplotlib && jupyter notebook

steps.title: Import libraries and load MNIST
steps.instructions: In your notebook, import tensorflow, layers, models, matplotlib.pyplot and numpy, then load MNIST with tf.keras.datasets.mnist.load_data() and divide both image arrays by 255. Run the cell (Shift+Enter).
hints: Use `tf.keras.datasets.mnist.load_data()` to unpack training and test tuples.
Cast pixel integers to `float32` before dividing by `255`.
Write `train_images = train_images.astype('float32') / 255` and do the same for `test_images`.
common_mistakes: Forgetting to normalize `test_images` as well as `train_images`.
steps.code:
import tensorflow as tf
from tensorflow.keras import layers, models
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

(train_images, train_labels), (test_images, test_labels) = tf.keras.datasets.mnist.load_data()
train_images = train_images.astype('float32') / 255
test_images = test_images.astype('float32') / 255

steps.title: Inspect shapes and plot digits
steps.instructions: Print the counts of train_images and test_images and the shape of train_images[0]. Use plt.subplots(1, 10, figsize=(10, 10)) to show the first 10 digits in grayscale with their labels, then run the cell.

targets.caption: Plot the first 10 training digits with labels

hints: Access `.shape[0]` on `train_images` and `test_images` for dataset sizes.
Loop `for i in range(10):` and call `axes[i].imshow(..., cmap='gray')`.
Set each subplot title with `axes[i].set_title(train_labels[i])` and hide axes with `axes[i].axis('off')`.
common_mistakes: Calling `plt.imshow` instead of `axes[i].imshow` inside the subplot loop.
Omitting `cmap='gray'` and rendering grayscale digits in the default viridis colormap.
steps.code:
print('Number of images in the training dataset:', train_images.shape[0])
print('Number of images in the testing dataset:', test_images.shape[0])
print('Shape of the images in the training dataset:', train_images[0].shape)

fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 10, figsize=(10, 10))
for i in range(10):
    axes[i].imshow(train_images[i].reshape(28, 28), cmap='gray')
    axes[i].set_title(train_labels[i])
    axes[i].axis('off')
plt.show()

steps.title: Define the sequential neural network
steps.instructions: Build `model` with models.Sequential: Flatten(input_shape=(28, 28, 1)), Dense 128 relu, Dense 64 relu, Dense 10 softmax. Run the cell (Shift+Enter).

explanations.topic: Feedforward architecture: 784 inputs, ReLU hidden layers, Softmax output

hints: Start by flattening the 28x28 image into a 784-element vector.
Stack `layers.Dense(128, activation='relu')` and `layers.Dense(64, activation='relu')`.
End with `layers.Dense(10, activation='softmax')` to output probabilities for digits 0-9.
common_mistakes: Using `'relu'` instead of `'softmax'` on the final 10-neuron output layer.
steps.code:
model = models.Sequential([
    layers.Flatten(input_shape=(28, 28, 1)),
    layers.Dense(128, activation='relu'),
    layers.Dense(64, activation='relu'),
    layers.Dense(10, activation='softmax')
])

steps.title: Compile and train the model
steps.instructions: Compile `model` with adam, sparse_categorical_crossentropy and accuracy metrics, then train with `history = model.fit(train_images, train_labels, epochs=5)`.

explanations.topic: Backpropagation and training loop over 60,000 images
Negative log likelihood / sparse categorical crossentropy loss

hints: Call `model.compile(...)` before calling `model.fit(...)`.
Use `loss='sparse_categorical_crossentropy'` since `train_labels` are integer digit indices.
Pass `train_images, train_labels, epochs=5` to `model.fit`.
common_mistakes: Using `categorical_crossentropy` instead of `sparse_categorical_crossentropy` when labels are integers rather than one-hot vectors.
steps.code:
model.compile(optimizer='adam',
              loss='sparse_categorical_crossentropy',
              metrics=['accuracy'])

history = model.fit(
    train_images,
    train_labels,
    epochs=5
)

steps.title: Predict and visualize one digit
steps.instructions: Define view_classify(image, probabilities), then run model.predict(image.reshape(1, 28, 28, 1)) on test_images[0] and pass the result to view_classify. Run the cell (Shift+Enter).
hints: `model.predict` expects a batch dimension even for a single image.
Reshape `image` to `(1, 28, 28, 1)` before passing it to `model.predict`.
Pass `probabilities[0]` (not `probabilities`) to `view_classify` so `barh` gets a 1D array of 10 values.
common_mistakes: Passing `image` directly to `model.predict` without reshaping to `(1, 28, 28, 1)`.
steps.code:
def view_classify(image, probabilities):
    fig, (ax1, ax2) = plt.subplots(figsize=(6,9), ncols=2)
    ax1.imshow(image)
    ax1.axis('off')
    ax2.barh(np.arange(10), probabilities)
    ax2.set_aspect(0.1)
    ax2.set_yticks(np.arange(10))
    ax2.set_yticklabels(np.arange(10))
    ax2.set_title('Class Probability')
    ax2.set_xlim(0, 1.1)
    plt.tight_layout()

image, label = test_images[0], test_labels[0]
probabilities = model.predict(image.reshape(1, 28, 28, 1))
view_classify(image, probabilities[0])

steps.title: Evaluate accuracy on test set
steps.instructions: Evaluate the trained model with `model.evaluate(test_images, test_labels)`, unpacking `test_loss` and `test_accuracy`. Print the percentage accuracy across all 10,000 test images.

targets.caption: Compute loss and accuracy on the test set

hints: `model.evaluate(test_images, test_labels)` returns a tuple of `(loss, accuracy)`.
Multiply `test_accuracy` by 100 and format with `:.2f` to print the percentage.
common_mistakes: Forgetting that `model.evaluate` returns both loss and accuracy, causing a `TypeError` when formatting.
steps.code:
test_loss, test_accuracy = model.evaluate(test_images, test_labels)
print(f'Accuracy of the neural network on the {test_images.shape[0]} test images: {test_accuracy * 100:.2f}%')
